lines.trans: Are we really flying up into the sky?
Of course we are. We're flying over Pearl Harbor in this.
Hold on—her manager is asking if we aren't filming on the ground.
That wouldn't have any impact, would it? We're shooting world-first footage.
Maybe you ought to stop him...
If the director says we shoot it, we do it. That's our job.
She says she's game to do it!
I knew she would say that.
Listen, this scene where you steal secret intelligence is the biggest highlight of the movie!
Alright, stand by for the final scene!
Yes, sir!
We're pulling off a scene nobody has ever done before!

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Noun.

examples.text: 今日は空がとても青いですね。
examples.trans: The sky is very blue today, isn't it?
Birds are flying in the sky.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

examples.text: まだ羽があるなら、ほら、逃げてみろよ。空へ飛んでけ！
examples.trans: If you've still got wings, go on, try escaping. Fly off into the sky!
Are we really flying up into the sky?

examples.text: 当たり前だろ。こいつで真珠湾の上を飛ぶ。
examples.trans: Of course we are. We're flying over Pearl Harbor in this.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

meanings.note: て-form 待って + ください is 'please wait'; causative お待たせして means 'having kept you waiting'.

examples.text: ちょっと待って、地上で撮るんじゃないの？って。
examples.trans: Hold on—her manager is asking if we aren't filming on the ground.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.

examples.text: それじゃ迫力が出ないだろ。世界初の映像を撮るんだ。
examples.trans: That wouldn't have any impact, would it? We're shooting world-first footage.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

examples.text: それじゃ迫力が出ないだろ。世界初の映像を撮るんだ。
examples.trans: That wouldn't have any impact, would it? We're shooting world-first footage.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.en: bring to a halt; shut off
meanings.note: Transitive verb for stopping a car, engine, or machine.

examples.text: ここに車を止めてください。
エンジンを止めました。

meanings.en: side or option in comparisons and advice (〜ほうがいい)
meanings.note: Paired with がいい after past or negative forms to recommend the better course ('it is better to...').

examples.text: 早く寝たほうがいいよ。
examples.trans: You had better go to sleep early.

examples.text: 傘を持ったほうがいいです。
examples.trans: It is better to bring an umbrella.

meanings.note: Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: First-person pronoun commonly used by men and boys in friendly or polite everyday settings.

examples.text: 僕もコーヒーをください。

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Everyday noun for one's job or workplace duties.

examples.text: 新しい仕事は楽しいです。
これから仕事に行きます。
examples.trans: I am heading to work now.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Compound noun.

examples.text: 今日はやる気が出ない。
やる気があれば何でもできる。
examples.trans: If you have motivation, you can do anything.

meanings.note: Colloquial particle adding emphasis, similar to でも or も.

examples.text: 俺だって言いたいことがある。
examples.trans: I have something I want to say too.

examples.text: 誰だって間違いはある。

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。
いいか、今からタイトルが出るシーンを撮影する。
examples.trans: Listen up, right now we're shooting the scene where the main title appears.

examples.text: いいか、このシーンは機密情報を奪う、この映画一番の見せ場だ！
examples.trans: Listen, this scene where you steal secret intelligence is the biggest highlight of the movie!

examples.text: 前人未到のシーンをやるぞ！
examples.trans: We're pulling off a scene nobody has ever done before!

examples.text: いいか、このシーンは機密情報を奪う、この映画一番の見せ場だ！
examples.trans: Listen, this scene where you steal secret intelligence is the biggest highlight of the movie!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.trans: Listen, this scene where you steal secret intelligence is the biggest highlight of the movie!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (一番近い), forms the superlative ('closest').

examples.trans: This one is the most popular.

examples.text: 一番近い駅はどこですか。

meanings.note: The most dramatic or impressive moment in a performance or story.

examples.text: いよいよ映画の見せ場だ。
examples.trans: At last, it's the highlight of the movie.

examples.text: ここが彼の見せ場です。
examples.trans: This is his moment to shine.

meanings.note: Satisfied exclamation when gearing up or finishing a task cleanly.

examples.text: よし、ラストシーンのスタンバイ！
examples.trans: Alright, stand by for the final scene!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.

examples.text: 前人未到のシーンをやるぞ！
examples.trans: We're pulling off a scene nobody has ever done before!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
